programme.title: People's Palaces: The Golden Age of Civic Architecture
programme.desc: Jonathan Foyle visits some of the most impressive neo-Gothic Victorian civic buildings in the north of England. Pointed arches, spires and clustered columns are present not only on churches and cathedrals, but also town halls and libraries, and the presenter explores the influence of architect Augustus Pugin and art critic John Ruskin in transferring the style from sacred to secular constructions

programme.title: Scotland: Rome's Final Frontier
programme.desc: Archaeologist Fraser Hunter reflects on three centuries of interaction and conflict between the Romans and ancient Scottish tribes. He examines whether the Scots were too strong for the invading army or if the country was simply considered not worth the effort of conquering. He also focuses on the first Tay Bridge, the first depiction of tartan and forgotten Roman camps that once held 35,000 men

programme.title: Treasures of the Anglo-Saxons
programme.desc: Historian Janina Ramirez investigates the development of Anglo-Saxon art. Examining the Sutton Hoo treasures the Franks Casket, the Staffordshire Hoard and the Lindisfarne Gospels, she uncovers the secret codes and symbols that reveal the pagan past and Christian future of the Anglo-Saxon people, and discusses how their artistic development was brought to an end by the Norman invasion of 1066

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.sub-title: Sunday in the Park with Stephen
programme.desc: Documentary originally broadcast in 1990, following Stephen Sondheim during his spell as visiting professor of drama at Oxford University. Cameras capture the composer taking students through the creative process of writing a musical. The film was made during rehearsals for the UK premiere of Sunday in the Park with George, which won the Olivier Award for best musical in 1991

programme.title: Stephen Sondheim's Old Friends
programme.desc: Cameron Mackintosh's stage production from May 2022, devised to celebrate Stephen Sondheim's talents as a composer and lyricist. Featuring an all-star cast including Michael Ball, Helena Bonham Carter, Rob Brydon, Petula Clark, Judi Dench, Haydn Gwynne, Bonnie Langford, Damian Lewis, Julia McKenzie, Bernadette Peters, Sian Phillips, Imelda Staunton and Gary Wilmot

programme.title: Sondheim at the BBC
programme.desc: A special tribute to Stephen Sondheim, featuring archive footage of performances of his songs by some of the world's biggest stars, taken from BBC shows over a period of 60 years. The programme includes clips of Shirley Bassey, Sammy Davis Jr, Michael Ball and Liza Minnelli

programme.title: People's Palaces: The Golden Age of Civic Architecture

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: Footage of some of the most breathtaking places on Earth, following the lives of some of the people who call these extraordinary places home. In the first episode, cameras follow yak-herder Thokmay Lowa as he leads his herd through one of the most treacherous mountain passes in the high Himalaya. Elsewhere, the programme follows members of Inuit communities in the Canadian Arctic as they take part in the hazardous mussel harvest, and people in Siberia searching for mammoth tusks, now released from the Siberian Permafrost after thousands of years

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: Lachlan Goudie explores how Scottish art has tackled questions of identity and taken on different ideas and styles over the past 100 years. He looks at how artists such as William McCance tried to bring about a 'Scottish Renaissance' in the visual arts, while the likes of Alan Davie and William Gear played a vital role in the revolutions of post-war art. He also meets Peter Doig, one of the world's most expensive living artists, to find out what it means to be a 'Scottish' artist today

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson hosts from the University of Salford with four contenders answering questions on the specialist subjects of English poetry of the First World War, the Glorious Revolution, the Allied armies in Italy in the Second World War, and the history of linguistics in the 19th and 20th centuries

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the final of the 1977 series of the quiz, with four contenders answering questions on the specialist subjects of the life of Francis Drake, the Roman Revolution 60 BC to 14 AD, Stuart kings and queens 1603-1714, and children's literature

programme.title: Saving Venice

programme.desc: Married couple Dexter and Aaron are looking for a fluffy, chunky dog. programme.title: Come Dine with Me

Cockapoodle Maggie wins the boys' hearts, but are her high energy levels and zesty personality too much for Marika and Jamie? programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo is in the glens of Antrim, where he is transfixed by tales of fairies and legends of the sea. programme.title: Mammals
programme.desc: From ice-covered seas to snow-capped mountains, mammals have conquered the cold, living in the harshest places on earth thanks to their remarkable intelligence and adaptations. The programme features polar bears on the Arctic islands of Svalbard, arctic foxes in Canada's Hudson Bay and snow leopards in the lofty mountains of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau in China

programme.title: James May's Big Trouble in Model Britain
programme.desc: Part one of two. Documentary following a year at British toymaker Hornby Hobbies as it teeters on the brink of collapse. Director Simon Kohler assesses the state of his beloved business after his four-year absence, while master modeller Jim is given the biggest build of his career

programme.title: James May's Big Trouble in Model Britain
programme.desc: Part two of two. Ken, head of audio development, is sent on a top-secret mission to capture the sound of a steam locomotive for its potential use in a new model, while marketing and development director Simon Kohler takes on two of his biggest rivals in a dramatic showdown. Plus, the company takes on its first female product designer in the shape of Caitlin Williams

programme.title: James May's Man Lab

The player who has won the least amount is then eliminated, and the last one standing competes for a £10,000 jackpot

programme.title: MasterChef USA
programme.desc: The Mystery Box is back - and it's every chef for themselves! The contestants must individually prepare a gourmet meal out of army rations

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles is in Bidford-on-Avon, Warwickshire, to meet Chloe, who has a rare genetic disorder that means she has to stay in the living room of her family's house under constant care. The DIY SOS team are joined by Laurence Llewelyn-Bowen and hundreds of Warwickshire volunteers to redesign the entire house to provide Chloe with independence, creating a self-contained apartment complete with bedroom, wet room and sitting room

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles, his team and a group of volunteers are in Monmouth, Wales, to transform the family home of Charlotte, a mother recovering from a stroke that left her with brain damage, speech loss and partial paralysis. The current layout of her home makes it difficult for Charlotte to move around and have her physiotherapy treatment, so the team redesign the house to make things easier for her, her husband Rob and their children

programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles travels to the Isle of Sheppey in Kent to meet two extraordinary dads, Garry and Kyle, who have adopted four vulnerable children - three of whom have special needs - to give them the best life possible. But their cramped three-bedroom bungalow is making family life difficult. So to give this family the space they so desperately need, the DIY SOS builders are undertaking their most ambitious project yet - to demolish the bungalow and build a bespoke five-bedroom house in its place. But with just nine days to complete the task, it looks like being their toughest one yet

programme.title: Inside the Ambulance
programme.desc: Paramedics attend a man with a possible ruptured appendix, an anxious 91-year-old with Covid, and a head injury case

programme.title: Inside the Ambulance
programme.desc: Crews attend a playground head injury, a patient with multiple fainting episodes, a man with suspected DVT, and visit a convent to treat a nun with chest pain

programme.title: Ambulance
programme.desc: Pete leads a team in the Tactical Operations Centre, responding to reports of an apparent shooting incident on a busy street in Clapham, south London, co-ordinating a response to reports of multiple casualties. Meanwhile, in the centre of the capital, crewmates Omar and Kez are dispatched to a motorbike crash outside Kilburn station and in Marylebone, attend to a patient who has slipped on the street and hit his head, which is now bleeding profusely. Narrated by Christopher Eccleston

programme.title: The Real Des: The Dennis Nilsen Story
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the personality of serial killer Dennis Nilsen, who murdered up to 15 young men, disposing of their bodies in his garden and down the drain

programme.title: 999 Rescue Squad
programme.desc: The team treat a lorry driver trapped behind his twisted steering wheel and help is urgently required for a 12-year-old who appears to be drunk after drinking an unknown substance

programme.title: Inside the Ambulance
programme.desc: Paramedics are sent to help a woman whose foot was run over by a bin lorry, and a team is sent to assess a man suffering from an agonising headache that has been going on for days.

programme.title: My Family
programme.desc: Susan is outraged when Ben, ever the romantic, buys her a vacuum cleaner for Christmas, so in a desperate attempt to make amends, he gets her a necklace instead. However, when he discovers it for sale at half the price the following day, he is determined to return it and buy it again at the bargain rate - but the no-nonsense jeweller (guest star Julian Clary) is having none of it. To make matters worse, Susan turns up and the Harpers end up getting trapped in the department store overnight. Meanwhile, Janey, Michael and Alfie decide to give Susan and Ben a thoughtful present for a change, but despite their best efforts, it does not turn out quite as planned. Robert Lindsay and Zoe Wanamaker star in the festive special from 2008

programme.title: Martin Clunes: Man to Manta

In Ecuador he meets ray expert Dr Andrea Marshall, and in Sri Lanka finds out that the creatures are being hunted by fishermen because of the use of their gills in Chinese medicine. Martin's dream finally comes true when he travels to the Maldives in the Indian Ocean and swims with 40 feeding mantas

programme.desc: Simon recalls some of the most dangerous experiences of his travels, from coming under fire in war-torn Mogadishu to squaring off with a female wrestler in Mexico City. Among the past destinations featured are a police cell in the far east of Russia, and the programme also looks back at his encounters with ambulance crews in San Salvador and anti-smuggling police in Italy

programme.title: Simon Reeve's South America
programme.desc: On the fourth leg of his journey through the continent, Simon travels through three of the world's most extreme environments as he takes in the salt flats of Bolivia, Brazil's Pantanal wetland region and Paraguay's Chaco Forest. In Bolivia, he meets a family making a living carving salt from the vast white expanse of the Uyuni flats, while in Brazil he has a close encounter with South America's apex predator, the jaguar. In Paraguay, Simon visits a Mennonites school, where traditionally clothed children are drilled in Bible texts and there are no smartphones to be seen

programme.title: Sacred Rivers with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The adventurer travels to China for a trip along the Yangtze, Asia's longest river and the third longest in the world. He follows the route to Dazu, where he sees 50,000 ancient rock carvings, some of the only religious artefacts not to have been destroyed under communist rule. He then takes a river cruise to the Three Gorges Dam - the biggest power station on the planet - before ending his journey in Shanghai, a shining symbol of China's new economic might and a city where many are rediscovering religious faith
